title: Fleet activation map: NA/EU/APAC vendor split and utilization plan
doc_text:
Purpose and scope:
This working sheet defines a phased activation map for GPU capacity across NA / EU / APAC for 2026 H1–2027 Q2. It focuses on vendor mix (cloud providers and preferred instance families), utilization targets, activation windows, gating criteria, and contingency/backfill options. This is intentionally operational (checklist + timeline) rather than a long-form strategy doc.

Summary (one-liner):
Staggered rollouts by region with mixed-vendor procurement to minimize supply risk and allow A/B validation of throughput and cost per token. Target steady-state utilization = 65% fleet-wide while preserving 20% buffer for burst and failover.

Assumptions (inputs used in forecasts):
- Typical request distribution: 55% short-chat (<128 tokens), 30% medium (128–512), 15% long (>512).
- Baseline per-GPU token throughput measured in lab: H100 80k tok/s equiv, A100 35k tok/s equiv, L4-like inference instances 18k tok/s equiv (relative, normalized).
- Regional latency SLOs: NA 90th < 120ms, EU 90th < 140ms, APAC 90th < 200ms (initial).
- Cold-cache startup KV-cache warming expected during first 14 days post-activation per region.
- Budget envelope for H1 2026 procurement: $11.5M committed capex/commit across providers.

Activation waves (high level):
- Wave 0 (canary): select customers and internal traffic, NA-central (1 AZ), A100-heavy reserved pool — target week of 2026-02-22.
- Wave 1: NA scale-out (multi-AZ across two clouds), add H100 reserved in limited qty — Mar–Apr 2026.
- Wave 2: EU primary launch (dual-cloud), mix A100 + L4-like for cost tier — Apr–May 2026.
- Wave 3: APAC soft-launch (single region initially), focus L4/edge instances for low-latency routing; add H100 for peak workloads — May–Jun 2026.
- Wave 4: Cross-region redundancy and capacity harmonization; full autoscale policies live — Jul–Sep 2026.

Per-region activation snapshot (target GPU counts by wave, reasoning):
- NA (primary market): initial fleet = 120 A100 equiv; phasing to 240 A100 equiv by end of Q3, target mix: 55% H100-equivalence by Q4 for peak models. Rationale: majority of traffic and earliest canary customers.
- EU: initial fleet = 60 A100 equiv, grow to 140 by Q4. Mix skewed to A100 + lower-cost L4 for embedding jobs. Rationale: regulatory zones require data locality and lower concurrency for some customers.
- APAC: initial fleet = 30 A100 equiv (L4-heavy), grow to 100 by Q1 2027. Rationale: spotty cloud availability and preference for smaller high-density instances to reduce cross-region egress.

Representative activation table (simplified):
Region | Wave start | Target GPU equiv (end-of-wave) | Primary vendor(s) | Util target (end-of-wave)
NA     | 2026-02-22 | 120 -> 240                     | AWS, GCP           | 60–70%
EU     | 2026-04-12 | 60 -> 140                      | GCP, Azure         | 55–65%
APAC   | 2026-05-24 | 30 -> 100                      | Azure, AWS (local) | 50–65%

Utilization policy:
- Cold rollout period (first 14 calendar days): allow utilization spike variance; throttle new customer onboardings until 7-day rolling average latency stables within 10% of baseline.
- Target steady-state utilization by region = median 65% across the busiest 6-hour window.
- Reserve buffer: maintain 18–22% spare capacity for burst and failure scenarios; automation triggers refill if buffer <15% for >30 minutes.

Model placement and hardware mapping:
- High-throughput models (long context, multi-turn chat): prefer H100-pinned pools in NA for latency-critical customers; fallback to A100 with reduced throughput at cost savings.
- Embedding workloads and batch inference: route to L4-equivalent/backfill pools in EU and APAC to reduce unit cost.
- Canary customers: pinned to canary pools that mirror production config but are isolated by routing policy.

Gating criteria for wave promotion (must be met before moving to next wave):
1) 7-day rolling P95 latency within SLO for 90% of routes.
2) End-to-end error rate <0.5% across critical routes for 48h.
3) Observed cost per 1M tokens within +/-10% of forecast for region.
4) KV cache hit-rate >= target (region-specific): NA 42%, EU 36%, APAC 30% after day-10.
5) Runbook validated: failover test exercised with <3 minute RTO for routing policies.

Risk register (top items and mitigations):
- Supply risk (preferred instance shortage): mitigation = vendor diversification + pre-negotiated burst credits on secondary provider.
- Unexpected high tail latency from shared tenancy: mitigation = progressive isolation (move high-tail routes into dedicated pools) + adaptive batching tuning.
- Cost overruns during onboarding: mitigation = strict auto-throttles + daily spend caps per region + rapid-rollover backfill to lower-cost SKU if overrun detected.
- KV cache cold start overruns: mitigation = synthetic warmup traffic during activation window; pre-warm most-used prefixes.

Contingency/backfill playbook (short):
- If buffer <12% for >1h in region -> immediate cross-region routing starting with lower-latency sibling (NA <-> EU where feasible), enable burst cluster in secondary vendor, alert infra lead.
- If observed 24h cost > forecast +15% -> pause non-critical pipelines (embedding batch, overnight retrain jobs), engage finance & product to gate new customer onboarding.

Operational runbooks to author before Wave 1:
- Region activation checklist (networking, KMS keys, VPC peering, subnets, NAT/GW checks).
- Cache warming script and safe-volume generation.
- Autoscaler tuning template by GPU SKU (min/max pods, target util).
- Billing guardrails: daily budget alert + emergency shutoff policy.

Telemetry and KPIs to track during rollouts (primary):
- P95 latency, P99 latency, error rate, per-token CPU/GPU utilization, KV-cache hit-rate, sustained queue depth, cost per 1M tokens, per-region egress cost.

Stakeholders and owners:
- Activation owner: Asha Mehta (infra lead)
- Fleet procurement & finance: Ben Liu
- On-call/runbook: Liam Rodriguez
- Product gating and customers: Priya Kapoor

Next immediate actions (this doc):
- Week 0 (by 2026-01-20): finalize vendor contract allocation table and submit ENGINFRA-7843 for procurement authorization.
- Week 1 (by 2026-01-26): create per-region network templates and get security review.
- Week 4 (by 2026-02-16): run canary dry-run with synthetic traffic and verify KV cache warmup pipeline.
- Track: add weekly cadence notes in Confluence page (linked) and sync with SRE runbook owners.

Open questions to resolve (short list):
- Exact H100:A100:L4 ratio per region at steady-state (propose to finalize by Feb 5 after vendor pricing update).
- Acceptable per-model degradation policy when routed to lower-tier SKUs.
- Whether to pre-warm local SSD-backed caches for EU customers beyond the standard warmup.

Notes and audit trail: this file is a working sheet, expect incremental edits. Use the linked Jira ENGINFRA-7843 and PR reference for change history. If any activation dates move, update the per-region snapshot and the gating checklist accordingly.

Appendix (quick numeric forecast snapshot):
- Expected committed GPUs by region (Q3 2026): NA 240 A100-equiv (with 120 H100 equiv), EU 140 A100-equiv (20% L4 batch), APAC 85 A100-equiv (40% L4-edge).
- Target fleet-wide steady util: 65% +/- 5%.
- Budget check: projected monthly run-rate (cloud commit + burst) at steady state = ~$1.95M/month.

Version notes: created 2026-01-12 by Asha Mehta. Last updated 2026-02-18 to reflect updated vendor pricing and minor timeline shifts.
